mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Captur 0.9 TCe engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Renault Captur 0.9 TCe engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£3,200 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £2,500-£4,500 depending on the engine code (H4Bt 400 vs H4Bt 444/447) and labour rates. Used engines: £550-£1,200. Reconditioned: £1,200-£2,300. Rebuilt with warranty: £1,800-£3,300. Fitting labour: 6-10 hours at £65-£100/hr.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Renault Captur 0.9 TCe?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is a rattling noise when starting a cold engine or under acceleration. Loss of power can also indicate timing system wear. The chain should last at least 100,000 miles with proper servicing, but can wear earlier with extended oil change intervals. Rattling noise on cold start. Loss of power. Rattling under acceleration. Complete engine failure if chain slips.

mainEntity.name: Does the Renault Captur 0.9 TCe have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 0.9 TCe (H4Bt) engine has a timing chain, not a belt. The chain should last at least 100,000 miles if the engine is properly serviced with annual oil and filter changes. However, extended oil change intervals (Renault's 30,000 km recommendation for some markets) can accelerate chain wear. Timing chain - not a belt. Annual oil changes are critical for chain longevity. Rattling noise indicates chain or tensioner wear.

mainEntity.name: Is the Renault Captur 0.9 TCe engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 0.9 TCe is generally a reliable and economical engine. However, it has a known weakness - the timing chain can wear prematurely, particularly with sporty driving and extended oil change intervals. With proper maintenance (annual oil changes using the correct specification oil), the engine can last 100,000+ miles without major issues. Generally reliable with proper maintenance. Timing chain wear is the primary concern. Annual oil changes are critical. Sporty driving accelerates chain wear.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 0.9 TCe engine codes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Captur 0.9 TCe was offered with several engine codes across its production life: H4Bt 400 (2013-2014, launch engine), H4Bt 408 (2014-2015, Stop & Start variant), H4Bt 444 (2015-2017, revised emissions) and H4Bt 447 (2017-2019, late Phase 1). All produce 90 hp and 135 Nm of torque. H4Bt 400: 2013-2014, launch engine. H4Bt 408: 2014-2015, Stop & Start. H4Bt 444: 2015-2017, revised emissions. H4Bt 447: 2017-2019, late Phase 1 variant.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Captur 0.9 TCe?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and what has failed. For a 2013-2019 Captur 0.9 TCe worth £3,000-£9,000, a £1,800-£3,200 rebuilt engine is usually worthwhile if the car is otherwise sound. Timing chain failure often makes replacement more cost-effective than repair. Cars worth £4,000+: rebuilt engine with warranty is recommended. Cars worth £2,000-£4,000: evaluate both options carefully. Timing chain failure: often cheaper to replace the engine than repair the damage. Cars worth under £2,000: consider used engine or scrap.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Captur 0.9 TCe - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The 0.9 TCe was the entry-level petrol engine for the first-generation Renault Captur, launched in 2013 as part of the Energy family of downsized turbocharged engines. This three-cylinder turbo petrol unit was developed jointly with Nissan and uses modern downsizing and turbocharging technologies. It remained available through the Phase 1 (2013-2019) generation, being replaced by the 1.0 TCe in the Phase 2 (2019-present) Captur.

milestones.description: H4Bt 400, 0.9-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol, 90 hp - launch engine for Captur, 5-speed manual
H4Bt 408, 0.9-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol, 90 hp - variant with Stop & Start technology
H4Bt 444, 0.9-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol, 90 hp - revised emissions calibration
H4Bt 447, 0.9-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol, 90 hp - late Phase 1 variant
0.9 TCe discontinued - replaced by 1.0 TCe (H4D) in Phase 2 Captur

commonProblems.h2: Renault Captur 0.9 TCe Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Captur 0.9 TCe is a generally economical and reliable entry-level engine, but it has a well-documented weakness - the timing chain system. Sporty driving and extended oil change intervals accelerate chain wear. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing components, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - The Most Common Renault Captur 0.9 TCe Problem
problems.affectedModels: Renault Captur 0.9 TCe (H4Bt 400, H4Bt 408, H4Bt 444, H4Bt 447)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain on the 0.9 TCe can stretch or wear prematurely. The chain should last at least 100,000 miles if the engine is properly serviced with annual oil and filter changes. However, sporty driving and extended service intervals accelerate wear. The timing chain can stretch or seize as early as around 60,000 kilometres (37,000 miles). A worn timing chain guide (slipper) can also cause rattling and eventually failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Visual inspection and tension check; listen for rattling on cold start
repairOptions.longevity: First step; recommended at every service
Recommended if rattling is heard or at 80k+ miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: If chain has slipped causing valve/piston damage
repairOptions.longevity: Catastrophic failure; often the only option

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2019 Captur 0.9 TCe is worth £3,000-£9,000 depending on mileage and condition. For a sub-£4,000 example, a £700-£1,100 timing chain replacement is a significant but justifiable repair. If the chain has failed causing engine damage, a rebuilt engine with warranty (£1,800-£3,200) may be the most cost-effective option.
problems.recommendation: Timing chain wear is the single most common issue facing Captur 0.9 TCe owners. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start or under acceleration, have the timing chain inspected immediately. Annual oil changes with the correct specification oil are critical - extended oil change intervals (Renault's 30,000 km recommendation for some markets) are a key contributor to premature chain wear. Preventative replacement at £700-£1,100 specialist cost is far cheaper than a full engine replacement at £1,800-£3,200.
problems.cta: -> Compare Renault Captur 0.9 TCe timing chain replacement costs

problems.h4: Loss of Power & Turbocharger Issues - Renault Captur 0.9 TCe
problems.rootCause: Turbocharger problems can cause loss of power, often accompanied by black smoke from the exhaust. The small turbo on the 0.9 TCe is sensitive to oil quality and change intervals. Vacuum leaks and manifold leaks can also cause power loss and are sometimes misdiagnosed as timing chain problems.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Identify and repair vacuum or intake leaks
If turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For most Captur 0.9 TCe examples, a £700-£1,200 turbo replacement is a justifiable repair. If the turbo has failed and sent debris through the engine, a rebuilt unit with warranty becomes the better option.
problems.recommendation: If you're experiencing loss of power, have the car properly diagnosed before assuming the engine needs replacement - vacuum and manifold leaks are common and much cheaper to fix than a timing chain or turbo replacement. Regular oil changes with the correct specification oil are critical for turbo longevity.

problems.rootCause: Like many small turbocharged engines, the 0.9 TCe can develop oil consumption issues at higher mileages. This is often related to piston ring wear or valve stem seal degradation.

repairOptions.longevity: If consumption is within acceptable limits
Labour-intensive but cheaper than full rebuild

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with upgraded piston rings

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Captur 0.9 TCe worth £3,000-£9,000, a £600-£1,000 valve stem seal replacement is a justifiable repair if the car is otherwise sound.
problems.recommendation: Oil consumption on higher-mileage 0.9 TCe engines is not uncommon. If your car is consuming more than 1 litre per 1,000 miles, have the engine inspected. A valve stem seal replacement at £600-£1,000 specialist cost is often more cost-effective than a full engine replacement.
